316244.literal:
Let $n$ be a positive integer and let $A\subset\mathbb Z_n$ be a set whose elements are all coprime to $n$. For a positive integer $k$, let $k\wedge A$ denote the set of sums of $k$ distinct elements of $A$.

**Fixed-length complete-sums conjecture.** If

$$
|A|\geq\sqrt{4n-4},
$$

then

$$
|k\wedge A|=n,
$$

where $k=\lceil\sqrt{n-1}\rceil$.

This is presented as a conjecture following the paper's main theorem and is not stated as proved; its status is therefore open.

316327.literal:
A **triangulation** is a simplicial decomposition of a closed orientable surface. A triangulation is **realizable in** $\mathbb{R}^3$ when its vertices can be embedded in $\mathbb{R}^3$ so that its edges are straight, its triangles are flat, and distinct simplices do not intersect except along shared faces.

**Geometric realization conjecture.** Every triangulation of a closed orientable surface of genus at most $4$ is realizable in $\mathbb{R}^3$ by straight edges, flat triangles, and without self-intersections.

The conjecture is true for spheres, but its natural extension to closed orientable surfaces of greater genus is false. The stated genus-at-most-four claim is therefore resolved as part of the known geometric realization results for triangulated surfaces.

316484.literal: Let $B_n$ be the braid group with generating set $\Sigma=\{\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_{n-1}\}$, and let $l_\Sigma(w)$ denote the $\Sigma$-length of a braid $w$. A braid word is **$\sigma$-consistent** if it is trivial, $\sigma$-positive, or $\sigma$-negative, where these notions are defined using the standard generators and their inverses. **Dynnikov–Wiest conjecture.** There are numbers $\lambda,c$ such that every braid $w\in B_n$ has a $\sigma$-consistent representative whose $\Sigma$-length is bounded linearly by the $\Sigma$-length of $w$; that is, the representative has length at most $\lambda l_\Sigma(w)+c$. The conjecture concerns whether the currently known exponential bound for such representatives can be replaced by a linear one. Its resolution is not supplied in the paper.

316626.literal:
Let $G$ be a permutation group and let $P(G)$ denote its permutation polytope. Let $B_n$ be the Birkhoff polytope.

**Birkhoff-polytope uniqueness conjecture.** If $P(G)$ is combinatorially equivalent to $B_n$ for some $n$, then $G$ is effectively equivalent to $S_n$.

The observation motivating the claim is that $B_3$ is realized by the full symmetric group $S_3$, which appears to be essentially the only such permutation group in that case. The general statement remains open.

Let $G$ be an abelian permutation group, let $P(G)$ be its permutation polytope, and write $|G|$ for the order of $G$.

**Affine-automorphism conjecture.** If

$$
|G|>2,
$$

then the group of affine automorphisms of $P(G)$ contains more elements than $G$.

For nonabelian groups, left and right multiplication already provide the motivating source of additional affine automorphisms. The assertion for abelian groups of order greater than two is presented as open.

318077.literal:
Let $\mathrm{G}$ be a perfect graph, and let $t$ be the relevant coloring parameter. The graph is **uniquely $t$-colorable** when it has a unique partition into $t$ color classes, while it is **sequentially $t$-colorable** when its vertices can be ordered so that, starting from a $t$-clique with distinct colors, each subsequent vertex receives a forced color by Tucker's sequential coloring rules.

**Tucker's conjecture.** For perfect graphs, unique $t$-colorability is equivalent to sequential $t$-colorability.

The equivalence is known in the supplied text for comparability graphs, complements of comparability graphs, chordal graphs, and complements of chordal graphs. The extension to all perfect graphs is presented as a conjecture, and no resolution is given here.

**Algebraicity conjecture.** Every $c\in\mathcal{S}$ is either an integer or an irrational algebraic number; equivalently,

$$
\mathcal{S}\subseteq\mathbb{Z}\cup(\mathbb{A}\setminus\mathbb{Q}).
$$

The conjecture is motivated by the fact that all speeds found in the paper are integers or algebraic irrationals. The supplied text gives no resolution.

381028.literal:
Let $J_{k,n}\in\mathcal P'_n$, for $k\in\mathbb Z_{n-1}$, be the union of the translate $(0,1)+\mathrm{NE}_{n-1}$, the product $\{n\}\times\mathbb Z_k$, and the set $\{(i,1):k<i<n\}$. Then

**The $J_{k,n}$ inner-product conjecture.**

$$
\langle \chi_{J_{k,n}},\chi_n\rangle=(-1)^{n-1}\binom{n}{k}\binom{n-2}{k-1}.
$$

This formula is proposed in connection with the preceding theorem and gives an explicit value for the inner product of the characteristic polynomial of $J_{k,n}$ with the Vandermonde polynomial $\chi_n$. The supplied text gives no resolution status or supporting results beyond presenting it as a proposed statement.
